The survival rate is not the issue that overwhelms the hospitals. It is the hospitalization rate that is the operative thing here. Whether the patient ultimately lives or dies is of little consequence. In some ways, a treatable illness makes a better weapon because it makes triage much harder since all patients survive with medical support.

For patients in the 65-74 year age range the hospitalization rate is a bit over 12%. That means if you have 1000 cases a day, roughly 121 more hospital beds are required each day. If that rate keeps up for a few weeks, the hospitals become swamped even if the average patient is only in 7 days. Add to that the ones who are hospitalized for longer periods and that adds up to the potential for people dying not because they have a deadly disease, but because they have a less serious disease, but no access to medical care.
